messages.text: I have a green card, got it 2 years ago. My kids were born here. Can my family get food stamps or Medicaid?

Yes, it's possible. I can check, but I need a few facts first.

1. Who lives with you and shares food? Please give each person's age. Tell me if anyone is pregnant, recently had a baby, or has a disability.
2. What is each person's income before taxes, and how often is it paid (weekly, every two weeks, or monthly)?

Your kids were born here, so they are U.S. citizens. They can often get help even when a parent's status needs a closer look. You can choose not to share your own status. A caseworker can check what applies to you.

Ok so me, my partner? No, it's just me and my two kids. I'm 32. Kids are 6 and 3. Nobody's pregnant or has a disability.

I make $1,800 a month before taxes. I get paid once a month.

Thanks, that helps. Two more questions:

1. How much is your rent or mortgage each month? Do you pay separately for heating or cooling, for other utilities like electric or water, or for only a phone?
2. Do you pay for child care so you can work? If so, how much each month?

I pay $850 a month for rent. Heat and cooling are separate, but I don't know the exact amount yet, so I'm not sure. No other utilities, just a phone I pay for myself. Electric is included in the rent.

No child care costs. The kids are in school and my neighbor watches them when I'm at work.

Your kids look likely to qualify for health coverage and WIC. Food assistance (SNAP) needs a caseworker to look at it. Only the state agencies decide, and you can apply for all three.

**TennCare/CoverKids (health coverage): likely for your kids**
- Your 6-year-old and your 3-year-old both look likely. Your income is $1,800 a month. The limit for a household of 3 is $3,028 for the 6-year-old and $3,233 for the 3-year-old.
- For you, a caseworker needs to look. Coverage for non-citizens depends on immigration status.
- Apply at [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701.
- Source: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html) (Division of TennCare).

**WIC: likely**
- WIC helps children under 5, so your 3-year-old fits. Your income is under WIC's limit of $4,212 a month for 3 people.
- Immigration status doesn't affect WIC in Tennessee.
- The clinic will do a short health and nutrition check.
- Apply at a local health department clinic, at [tn.gov/health/wic](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html), or call 1-800-342-5942.
- Sources: [USDA WIC income limits, July 2026 to June 2027](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926) and [7 CFR 246.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.7).

**Food assistance (SNAP): a caseworker needs to look at this**
- Non-citizen rules for SNAP changed in 2025 and depend on your immigration status, so I can't say how they apply to you. Your U.S.-born kids can still get SNAP.
- Your income and costs look within the limits for a household of 3. If everyone counted, the screening would show about $658 a month. That is only a rough estimate. Your real amount could be different if your status affects who counts.
- You don't need your exact heating and cooling bill. SNAP uses a standard amount for it. The screening used older figures because newer ones weren't available yet.
- Savings matter too. The federal limit is $3,000 in cash and bank accounts.
- Apply through [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287.
- Sources: [USDA SNAP eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility) and [USDA's 2026-27 limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola).

**Next steps**
- Apply for all three. You can apply for your kids even if your own status needs a closer look.
- For free local help with applying, dial **211**.
- For questions about your green card and these programs, a caseworker or a legal aid group can check what applies to you.
